You wake up, and your phone is full of messages nobody sent. Your boss typed,
Then deleted it. Your mum typed,
Eleven times. And at three a.m., your best friend typed three words… and held backspace.
She never sent it. You could answer anyway.

They look like normal messages. Just grey. And they flicker, like they're still deciding. Everything anyone almost said to you since midnight. Two hundred and twelve. Before breakfast. The pizza place wrote,
Then sent a coupon instead. The group chat is worse.
Is he bringing the guitar again?
Nobody tells you. Tonight, the guitar stays home.
In the lift, a stranger types,
You stand a little taller anyway.
At work, it turns out to be useful.
I was… just about to ask.
Could you cover Friday? No. Forget it.
By lunch, you're answering questions nobody asked. It feels like kindness.
Should I warn him about the budget?
Is something wrong with the budget?
It doesn't feel like kindness to them. By three, people turn their phones face down when you walk past.
No, no. I just had lunch. A real one. Vegetables and everything.
Why are you telling me this?
I did. I did want to know.
That one, you got right. You answered. And she never knew you'd read it.
All afternoon, one message sits at the top of the pile. You don't open it. You don't need to.
Fine! Tired. You know. Fine. How was work?
Weird. People kept hiding their phones.
Maybe stop reading over their shoulders.
Above her phone. Grey. Still flickering.
You've had the perfect reply ready all day. You type it under the table.
She didn't send it. That was a decision. Hers.
You hold backspace. Now there are two unsent messages at this table.
Want to split a cinnamon roll?
You talk about nothing. Twenty minutes of nothing.
Three words. Out loud. Sixteen hours late, and exactly on time.
I didn't get it. The second interview. I've been saying fine for a week.
That's a long time to say fine.
On the way home, your phone buzzes. A real one, this time.
